text:
incident-bot: PAGER: smart-routing errors detected in eu-west & eu-central regions. 20% request error rate vs baseline <1%. Trigger: route-fallbacks to legacy-edge triggered repeatedly. Alert level: P1.
ashley: acked. I'm oncall for infra — joining.
sre-jordan: seeing 502/503 spikes from the edge. Errors originate after our smart-router returns a failing geo-variant, then fallback to another region which also times out. Looks like a routing flap.
infra-kim: digging into DNS/VIP layer first. Running quick dig from multiple regions.
eng-ops-lee: adding runbook links: https://runbooks.internal/smartroute-fallbacks and the routing-policy doc.
infra-kim: output (from eu-west dig):
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood-inference.eu-west.example
10.12.200.45
10.12.200.46
```
and from gir-ldn (another resolver):
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood-inference.eu-west.example @8.8.8.8
10.12.200.45
```
but from a handful of probes we still see stale rrsets pointing to old-hosts: `10.9.1.12` which were decommissioned last month. TTL on those records is high (300s) on some recursors.
sre-jordan: confirmed — some upstream recursors returning stale rrsets. This causes smart-router health checks to mark regional pool unhealthy when requests hit the stale IPs and time out; then policy tries next region and oscillates.
oncall-matt: paging oncall lead. What's customer impact?
customer-success-jeremy: multiple customers reporting increased latency and 5xx for generation endpoints in EU, about ~8% of requests failing intermittently. A few enterprise customers hit SLA thresholds. We're coordinating incident comms.
ashley: live mitigation plan: 1) temp change smart-routing fallback policy to remove strict probing on health checks (so we avoid immediate failover oscillation), 2) push small TTL override (lower to 30s) for edge A records in control plane, 3) trigger cache purge on major recursors (where we can), 4) add IP allowlist fallback to known-good regional hosts.
eng-ops-lee: proposing a quick policy patch (canary) — set fallback.cooldown to 60s and require 3 consecutive probe failures to flip. YAML snippet:
```
# quick canary change
routing_policy:
  failover:
    consecutive_failures: 3
    cooldown_seconds: 60
```
infra-kim: applying DNS TTL override in control plane now (reduces advertised TTL to 30s). Propagation will vary by resolver. Kicking off recursor cache purge requests for major providers.
sre-jordan: running healthcheck against known-good host pool to validate service: `curl -v http://10.12.200.45/health` — 200 OK; `curl` to stale host `10.9.1.12` times out.
ashley: temporarily pin smart-router for EU traffic to eu-west-primary pool via policy rollout id `rollout/196543-quickpin` to stop cross-region traffic while DNS clears. This should reduce customer impact but will reduce capacity ~25% in region.
pm-anjali: approve capacity risk. Customer comms: ETA for mitigation 20-30m, will update in 15.
infra-kim: cache purge responses: CloudProvider-A acknowledged, CloudProvider-B requires support ticket (submitted). Some ISPs still holding stale entries, we see recursors in trace returning the old IP.
oncall-matt: oncall handoff note — if oscillation resumes after TTL change, switch to manual pin to healthy IPs and escalate to networking on-call.
sre-jordan: executing traffic validation from synthetic journey: 50 probes across EU -> success rate jumped from 82% -> 98% after policy canary + TTL override. Latency improving.
customer-success-jeremy: started proactive emails to impacted customers with status and temporary mitigation. No data exposure.
eng-ops-lee: pushing a small telemetry flag to track routing-change events for the next 1h to detect re-flaps.
ashley: follow-up tasks: 1) postmortem owner (sre-jordan), 2) add guardian test to repo that detects stale DNS rrsets before decommissioning hosts, 3) review default TTLs and smart-router sensitivity.
sre-jordan: taking postmortem. Early root cause hypothesis: decommissioned host IPs remained cached in some public/enterprise resolvers; combined with aggressive smart-router single-probe failover logic caused cross-region fallback oscillation and customer impact.
infra-kim: filed ticket with ISP list: TICKET-4821, will track cache eviction via provider support threads.
eng-ops-lee: timeline note for RCA: record exact timestamps of policy flips, DNS changes, and cache purge acknowledgements.
oncall-matt: handing off monitoring to next oncall at +2h (oncall-matt -> oncall-ashley). If error rate creeps above 5% re-alert P1.
ashley: ack handoff. leaving console dashboards open, will be reachable on Slack.
pm-anjali: drafting customer incident summary for external comms.
sre-jordan: preliminary mitigation confirmed. Closing active mitigation channel in 40m if stable; won't close incident until RCA posted.
customer-success-jeremy: logged impacted customers and updated case trackers.
incident-bot: NOTE: incident status changed to mitigated (partial) at 1965432250.
eng-ops-lee: misc ops note: when we re-enable the sensitivity of smart-router, we'll rollout in 2 phases: internal canary -> 5% prod -> 25% -> 100% over 4h.
sre-jordan: postmortem checklist: include timeline, contributing factors (DNS TTL policy, decommission process, smart-router thresholds), and follow-ups with networking team to add pre-decomm DNS cache invalidation.
ashley: thanks everyone.
pm-anjali: leaving for the day, will follow RCA tomorrow.
incident-bot: thread archived by incident-bot at 1965432345.
